paper_title: Constraints on Axion-like Particles from a Hard $X$-ray Observation of Betelgeuse
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 3 (95% C.L. upper limit)
notes: First hard X-ray (NuSTAR, 50 ks) search for ALPs produced in Betelgeuse's core and reconverted in the Galactic magnetic field. The 95% C.L. limit depends on the stellar model (time to core collapse tcc) and assumed transverse Galactic B-field (0.4-3.0 uG): g_agamma < 1.8e-11 GeV^-1 for m_a < 3.5e-11 eV (most conservative: tcc=1.55e5 yr, BT=0.4 uG), down to g_agamma < 5.2e-12 GeV^-1 for m_a < 5.5e-11 eV (most optimistic: tcc=3.6 yr, BT=3.0 uG). I encode the CONSERVATIVE mass-independent bound as a flat line spanning ~1e-14 eV (low-mass edge of Fig. 1/3 plots) up to the stated validity mass 3.5e-11 eV; the limit weakens at higher masses but no numerical values are tabulated. Not a dark-matter haloscope, so no local DM density assumed.
